items.title: Spatially-Augmented Sequence-to-Sequence Neural Diarization for Meetings
items.authors: Li Li(Whuan University; The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen); Ming Cheng(Whuan University); Juan Liu(Whuan University); Ming Li(Whuan University; The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen)
items.abstract: This paper proposes a Spatially-Augmented Sequence-to-Sequence Neural Diarization (SA-S2SND) framework, which integrates direction-of-arrival (DOA) cues estimated by SRP-DNN into the S2SND backbone. A two-stage training strategy is adopted: the model is first trained with single-channel audio and DOA features, and then further optimized with multi-channel inputs under DOA guidance. In addition, a simulated DOA generation scheme is introduced to alleviate dependence on matched multi-channel corpora. On the AliMeeting dataset, SA-S2SND consistently outperforms the S2SND baseline, achieving a 7.4% relative DER reduction in the offline mode and over 19% improvement when combined with channel attention. These results demonstrate that spatial cues are highly complementary to cross-channel modeling, yielding good performance in both online and offline settings.

items.title: Bidirectional Retention Network-based Segmentation Model for Speaker Diarization
items.authors: Jian You(Cisco Systems); Xiangfeng Li(Cisco Systems); Tengfei Zhou(Cisco Systems); Erwan Zerhouni(Cisco Systems)
items.abstract: End-to-end neural diarization with vector clustering (EEND-VC) has emerged as a robust solution for real-world applications due to its ability to handle overlapped speech and an arbitrary number of speakers. Existing EEND-VC segmentation back ends typically employ recurrent neural networks (RNNs), attention-based architectures, or Mamba. In this paper, we propose a novel segmentation model that integrates a WavLM-based front end with a bidirectional Retention Network (BiRetNet) back end. RetNet provides dual parallel and recurrent formulations with favorable computational scaling with respect to sequence length, motivating its use as a promising segmentation back end for speaker diarization. We evaluate the potential of BiRetNet by benchmarking it against established RNN, attention, and Mamba-based variants. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms these baselines, achieving state-of-the-art performance on two widely used diarization datasets.

items.title: Role-Aware Semi-Supervised Domain Adaptation for Teacher-Student Speaker Diarization
items.authors: Zhen Liao(Huazhong University of Science and Technology); Gaole Dai(Huazhong University of Science and Technology); Weiwei Jiang(Huazhong University of Science and Technology); Mengting Wang(Huazhong University of Science and Technology); Wei Xu(Huazhong University of Science and Technology)
items.abstract: Speaker diarization identifies anonymous speakers, yet educational settings require role-based segregation (teacher vs. student). Generic models struggle here due to data scarcity and domain shifts. We propose a Mean Teacher-based Role-Aware Semi-Supervised Domain Adaptation framework using our proposed TSSD, a semi-supervised dataset. By exploiting unlabeled target-domain data, our method aligns generic acoustic priors with classroom distributions. To drive this adaptation, we propose Role-Aware Union Loss that reformulates the task from identity distinction to role detection, enabling fine-grained separation via coarse supervision to resolve overlapping ambiguity without explicit IDs. we also adopt PIT-MSE consistency loss to enforce robust student-teacher model alignment invariant to speaker ordering. Experiments show our method disentangles complex acoustic scenes into distinct role-based streams, offering a scalable solution for "many-to-one" mapping in conversational analysis.

items.title: Leveraging Diarization Labels for Robust Score Calibration in Target Speaker Tagging via Gaussian Mixture Modeling
items.authors: Hee-Soo Heo(NAVER Cloud Corporation); Minjae Lee(NAVER Cloud Corporation); Youngki Kwon(NAVER Cloud Corporation); Han-Gyu Kim(NAVER Cloud Corporation); Bong-Jin Lee(NAVER Cloud Corporation)
items.abstract: Target speaker tagging (TST) diarizes multi-speaker audio and assigns enrolled speaker identities to the resulting segments. However, the short duration of many diarized segments leads to unreliable verification scores with high variance. While aggregating scores across co-labeled segments within a session offers a potential remedy, naive averaging is inherently fragile under erroneous diarization labels. We propose a calibration method based on a two-component Gaussian mixture model (GMM) fitted to the score distribution within each diarization cluster. One component captures correctly clustered segments and the other absorbs misclustered ones. Each segment is assigned the mean of its most probable component, enabling robust aggregation that is resilient to diarization errors. Experiments on TST-Bench and the ICSI Meeting Corpus demonstrate consistent improvements over uncalibrated scoring and conventional baselines across multiple operating points and embedding architectures.

items.title: SphereVBx: Spherical Variational Bayes Clustering for Simplified EEND-VC Diarization
items.authors: Petr Pálka(Brno University of Technology); Jiangyu Han(Brno University of Technology); Prachi Singh(Brno University of Technology); Marc Delcroix(NTT, Inc.); Naohiro Tawara(NTT, Inc.); Lukáš Burget(Brno University of Technology)
items.abstract: We propose SphereVBx, a Bayesian clustering framework for hyperspherical embeddings based on Toroidal Probabilistic Spherical Discriminant Analysis (T-PSDA). The method follows the variational Bayesian formulation of VBx while replacing the Gaussian Probabilistic Linear Discriminant Analysis (PLDA) backend with T-PSDA, resulting in variational inference in a mixture of von Mises-Fisher distributions. We apply SphereVBx to speaker diarization and in particular to the end-to-end neural diarization with vector clustering (EEND-VC) framework. A parameter-free variant, denoted SphereVBx-PF, corresponds to a spherical similarity model closely related to cosine scoring and does not require pretrained backend parameters. Experiments on multiple diarization benchmarks show that SphereVBx improves clustering accuracy in cascaded diarization pipelines and achieves comparable or better performance in the EEND-VC framework while significantly simplifying its clustering stage.

items.title: Indic DiarBench: A Multilingual Joint Diarization and ASR Benchmark for Indian Languages
items.authors: Deovrat Mehendale(Sarvam AI); Aditya Mehndiratta(Sarvam AI); Dhruv Rathi(Sarvam AI); Kaushal Bhogale(IIT Madras); Mitesh M. Khapra(IIT Madras)
items.abstract: In this work, we introduce Indic DiarBench, a speaker diarization and ASR benchmark dataset spanning all 22 scheduled languages of India. This corpus comprises approximately 108 hours of natural multi-speaker audio from near-field meetings, far-field recordings, and in-the-wild audios. All annotations are human-corrected with time-aligned speaker attributed transcriptions. The dataset captures conversational nuance prevalent in Indian speech, such as English code-mixing, dialectal variation, and frequent speaker overlap. To establish a baseline for joint ASR and diarization capabilities we evaluate leading systems including commercial speech APIs and multimodal large language models. Indic DiarBench is released as an open-access resource to advance inclusive, multilingual speech technology research for Indian languages.

items.title: Speaker Separation via Audio Language Modeling
items.authors: Luca Lanzendörfer(ETH Zurich); Constantin Pinkl(ETH Zurich); Florian Grötschla(ETH Zurich); Roger Wattenhofer(ETH Zurich)
items.abstract: We propose LlaSep, an autoregressive approach for speaker separation. LlaSep uses discrete audio tokens with a causal language model to generatively separate mixed speech signals. Unlike existing methods that rely on continuous spectral representations and task-specific components our system operates entirely in the discrete token domain. LlaSep generates per-speaker codec token streams in a single decoding pass, conditioned on the tokenized mixture and semantic features from a pretrained speech encoder. LlaSep is trained via supervised fine-tuning on ground-truth speaker tokens from a large-scale synthetic multilingual conversation dataset spanning seven languages and 15k hours. Evaluation on LibriCSS and CallHome demonstrates competitive separation and diarization performance and substantially higher audio quality compared to previous baselines, demonstrating that token-level language modeling is a viable paradigm for multi-speaker speech processing.

items.title: RT-ASDNet: Unified, Real-Time Active Speaker Detection
items.authors: Okan Köpüklü(Microsoft)
items.abstract: Existing audio-visual active speaker detection methods often rely on multi-stage pipelines or computationally expensive temporal modeling, limiting their applicability in real-time scenarios. In this paper, we propose RT-ASDNet, a unified, end-to-end audio-visual architecture for real-time active speaker detection. Our approach jointly processes raw audio waveform and video frames through two specialized streams that are fused into an anchor-free detection head, simultaneously localizing faces and predicting speaking activity in a single forward pass. Unlike multi-stage approaches that require separate face detection, feature extraction, and classification steps, RT-ASDNet performs joint localization and classification within a unified framework, significantly reducing inference latency and pipeline complexity. Moreover, since inference is performed only once per frame, the computational cost remains constant regardless of the number of people in the scene. We evaluate our method on the AVA-ActiveSpeaker benchmark and set the baseline for joint detection and classification on active speaker detection task.

items.title: Joint Learning Global-Local Speaker Classification to Enhance End-to-End Speaker Diarization and Recognition
items.authors: Yuhang Dai(Northwestern Polytechnical University; Soul AI Lab); Haopeng Lin(Soul AI Lab); Jiale Qian(Soul AI Lab); Ruiqi Yan(Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Hao Meng(Soul AI Lab); Hanke Xie(Northwestern Polytechnical University; Soul AI Lab); Hanlin Wen(Soul AI Lab); Shunshun Yin(Soul AI Lab); Ming Tao(Soul AI Lab); Xie Chen(Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Lei Xie(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Xinsheng Wang(Soul AI Lab)
items.abstract: Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance in end-to-end speaker diarization and recognition. However, their speaker discriminability remains limited due to the scarcity of large-scale conversational data and the absence of explicit speaker representation optimization. To address this, we propose GLSC-SDR, a paradigm that jointly trains speaker classification with diarization and recognition. We further introduce a Global-Local Speaker Classification strategy, which uses clustered speakers as global labels and re-encoded intra-cluster speakers as local labels. This hierarchical design enhances fine-grained speaker discrimination while preserving semantic transcription accuracy. Experiments on AliMeeting, AISHELL-4, and AMI-SDM demonstrate that GLSC-SDR achieves competitive or superior performance compared to simulation-based and multi-encoder approaches, without relying on large-scale real conversational data.

items.title: POP-SED: Prototype Orthogonal Projection for Robust Few-shot Sound Event Detection
items.authors: Takehiko Kagoshima(Toshiba Corporation)
items.abstract: Few-shot sound event detection (SED) must operate with limited examples that often contain overlapping background sounds, making robust detection challenging. We present prototype orthogonal projection for SED (POP-SED), a fine-tuning-free method that suppresses background influences by projecting the target-event prototype onto a subspace orthogonal to background vectors. Background vectors are obtained by fitting a von Mises-Fisher mixture model to features from background and query intervals, and then selecting a subset of mean vectors that maximizes a robustness-aware support-set criterion. On the DCASE2024 Task 5 validation set, POP-SED achieved an F-score of 62.35% without any fine-tuning, approaching the accuracy of top-performing systems that require both domain-level and support-set fine-tuning.

items.title: CLEAR: Clinical LLM Embedding and Attention-based Reconstruction
items.authors: Eashita Wazed(Chonnam National University); Hieyong Jeong( Chonnam National University); Choonsung Shin(Chonnam National University); Shima Okada(Ritsumeikan University)
items.abstract: Clinical heart sound analysis is vital for cardiovascular diagnosis but is frequently disrupted by non-stationary noise. To overcome the limitations of traditional methods, we propose CLEAR: Clinical LLM Embedding and Attention-based Reconstruction. Given noisy audio, a pretrained Whisper encoder extracts high-dimensional semantic embeddings. A Graph Attention Network (GAT) models these as graph nodes to predict latent masks, isolating pure heart sounds. A Latent Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) then refines these representations to generate distortion-free signals. Evaluated under 10 dB SNR environmental noise, CLEAR demonstrated an exceptional peak restoration capability, achieving a maximum PESQ of 4.64 and SI-SDR of 64.35 dB from severely degraded inputs (PESQ 1.03, SI-SDR -29.37 dB). By delivering natural, artifact-free audio, CLEAR significantly enhances clinical auscultation and early disease detection.

items.title: Few-shot Class-variable Incremental Audio Classification via Prototype Adaptation and Pseudo Class-variable Training
items.authors: Yanxiong Li(South China University of Technology); Guoqing Chen(South China University of Technology); Qianqian Qianqian Li(South China University of Technology); Sen Huang(South China University of Technology)
items.abstract: In the task of few-shot class-incremental audio classification, the number of classes is assumed to always increase without considering the possibility of decrease. However, the number of classes generally increases or decreases in practice. In this paper, we investigate a problem of Few-shot Class-variable Incremental Audio Classification (FCIAC), where the number of classes increases or decreases. We propose a FCIAC method using prototype adaptation and pseudo class-variable training. The model in our method consists of an encoder and a classifier. The classifier is initialized by a class-variable prototype adaptation network, whose structure dynamically changes with the change of classes. In addition, we design a pseudo class-variable training strategy to enhance the model’s adaptability to changing classes. Experiments on three public datasets show that our method exceeds previous methods in average accuracy. The code is at: https://github.com/cgq2971-afk/FCIAC.

items.title: Quality Adaptive Angular Margin Learning for Respiratory Sound Classification
items.authors: Yoon Tae Kim(RSC LAB, MODULABS); Heejoon Koo(RSC LAB, MODULABS); Miika Toikkanen(RSC LAB, MODULABS); June-Woo Kim(Wonkwang University)
items.abstract: We present a quality-adaptive angular-margin learning framework that improves feature generalization by enforcing intra-class compactness and inter-class separability. Our framework, titled QLung, introduces a no-reference audio quality margin derived from spectral entropy and root-mean-square energy, which adaptively scales angular margins based on recording quality. To this end, we propose a log-scaled angular margin that stabilizes training under severe class imbalance. We also use an angular classifier that normalizes features and class weights, ensuring margin penalties are applied consistently on the unit hypersphere. Our approach improves in-distribution performance on the ICBHI dataset by 2.46% over the cross-entropy baseline, and most significantly, achieves the strongest out-of-distribution performance on the SPRSound dataset compared to prior state-of-the-art methods. Code is available at https://github.com/RSC-Toolkit/QLung.

items.title: Fair Cognitive Impairment Detection Through Unlearning
items.authors: William Nguyen(University of Massachusetts Lowell); Jiali Cheng(University of Massachusetts Lowell); Hadi Amiri(University of Massachusetts Lowell)
items.abstract: Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) is a medical condition characterized by a noticeable decline in memory, language, or thinking abilities. MCI detection from spontaneous speech is promising for scalable screening. However, learned models often exploit demographic cues correlated with labels, resulting in a large performance gap across subgroups. We present a multi-modal framework that combines (i) cross-model fusion between modalities (speech, text, and image), and (ii) unlearning using gradient reversal that discourages the shared embedding from encoding task-irrelevant demographic attributes. Evaluated on the multilingual benchmarks TAUKADIAL and PREPARE, our method outperforms the state-of-the-art multilingual and multi-modal baseline in MCI classification while substantially reducing the performance gap across patient subgroups (sex and language). We further analyze transfer across datasets, showing that demographic unlearning helps learn more robust representations for MCI detection.

items.title: QuadVAD: Fine-Grained Speech Detection with a Compact Architecture
items.authors: Ramakrishna Chaitanya Rachumallu(Meeami Technologies); Nivedita Chennupati(Meeami Technologies); Ankit Gupta(Meeami Technologies); Balaji Padmanaban(Meeami Technologies); ParvathiPriyanka Bolla(Meeami Technologies); Harish Rajamani(Meeami Technologies); Naveen Ambati(Meeami Technologies)
items.abstract: Voice Activity Detection (VAD) is the foundational gatekeeper of the power-performance envelope in always-on edge devices and conversational AI systems. An ideal VAD must provide ultra-low algorithmic latency for barge-in and end-of-turn detection, maintain noise robustness, and minimize computation and footprint for edge deployment. We propose QuadVAD, a highly optimized, small-footprint neural VAD operating at a fine-grained 4 ms resolution. An efficient data synthesis and alignment pipeline leveraging Montreal Forced Aligner and fine-tuning on the TIMIT Acoustic-Phonetic Corpus ensures precise boundary detection. Experiments show improved onset detection with QuadVAD. The architecture combines convolutional blocks with an LSTM Cell, totaling 25 KB and achieves an RTF of 0.0014 on a 13th Gen Intel Core i7 laptop. QuadVAD effectively balances latency, robustness, size and compute, making it well suited for deployment in conversational AI systems and always-on speech interfaces.

items.title: Exploratory analysis of yellow mongoose vocalization: detection from in-the-wild recordings and call classification
items.authors: Sevada Hovsepyan(Idiap Research Institute); Imen Ben Mahmoud(Idiap Research Institute); Vanessa Rüegg(University of Zurich); Marta Manser(University of Zurich); Mathew Magimai.-Doss(Idiap Research Institute)
items.abstract: Understanding the vocal repertoire of social animals, such as the yellow mongoose (YM), is crucial for deciphering their social structure and evolutionary history. In this study, we present an exploratory analysis of YM vocalization detection and classification using both signal processing and machine learning approaches. The analysis uses two distinct datasets: (1) expert-annotated, clean pup vocalizations (n=940), and (2) noisy field recordings (n=29) captured with directional microphones. Our results indicate that handcrafted features, originally developed for human speech modeling to represent syllables, are effective for animal vocalization classification, suggesting potential shared acoustic structures. Although detecting YM vocalizations in wild recordings proved challenging, our objective is to aid annotators by flagging potential vocalization segments. The results presented in this work provide a foundation for scalable, semi-automated analysis of animal vocal repertoires.

items.title: Continual Generalized Category Discovery for Acoustic Signals via Instance-Adaptive Regularization and Dynamic Teacher Guidance
items.authors: Qisheng Xu(National University of Defense Technology; National Key Laboratory of Parallel and Distributed Computing); Shanhao Han(National University of Defense Technology; National Key Laboratory of Parallel and Distributed Computing); Hui Geng(National University of Defense Technology; National Key Laboratory of Parallel and Distributed Computing); Yulu Fang(National University of Defense Technology; National Key Laboratory of Parallel and Distributed Computing); Yunsheng Xiong(National University of Defense Technology; National Key Laboratory of Parallel and Distributed Computing); Yutao Dou(Hunan University); Kele Xu(National University of Defense Technology; National Key Laboratory of Parallel and Distributed Computing)
items.abstract: Acoustic perception systems must continually adapt to emerging sound categories, yet real-world annotation is often unavailable or costly. Continual Generalized Category Discovery (C-GCD) addresses this challenge by retaining previously learned classes while discovering novel categories from unlabeled streaming data. However, directly transferring vision-based C-GCD methods to audio leads to marked performance degradation because acoustic signals exhibit complex spectrotemporal structures, strong class overlap, and severe base-class bias. We therefore propose an audio-oriented C-GCD framework with instance-adaptive regularization to balance consolidation and exploration, GMM-based adaptive thresholding, and an EMA-updated dynamic teacher for stable pseudo-label generation. Experiments on LibriSpeech and ShipsEar show consistent gains in novel-class discovery and old-class retention. On ShipsEar, our method achieves 74.14% cumulative average accuracy, surpassing Happy by 4.84 percentage points.

items.title: I'll Keep an Ear Out: Teaching AudioLLMs Proactive Audio Assistance
items.authors: Amit Kumar Singh Yadav(Meta Reality Labs); Ritvik Shrivastava(Meta Reality Labs); Xuan Zhang(Meta Reality Labs); Seungwhan Moon(Meta Reality Labs); Shashank Jain(Meta Reality Labs); Pinar Donmez(Meta Reality Labs); Babak Damavandi(Meta Reality Labs)
items.abstract: Audio large language models (AudioLLMs) operate reactively, responding only when queried. We introduce proactive audio assistance, where an AudioLLM monitors an audio stream and autonomously decides when to alert the user from a single natural-language intent, motivated by wearable applications for Deaf and Hard of Hearing users. We propose Interrupt and Silent Modeling (ISM), a model-agnostic paradigm that embeds proactive decisions into LLM decoding via two special tokens: and , capturing four states: onset detection, sustained-relevance triggering, irrelevance suppression, and de-duplication. Applied to Qwen2-Audio-7B, ISM achieves 99.6% interrupt F1 and perfect de-duplication recall on ESC-50. On noisy Epic-Sounds kitchen audio, ISM achieves the highest interrupt F1 without domain-specific training, the only method maintaining strong onset detection without over-triggering or over-suppression. Streaming evaluation confirms real-time viability with 3.5-second average latency.

items.title: STSR: High-Fidelity Speech Super-Resolution via Spectral-Transient Context Modeling
items.authors: Jiajun Yuan(Wuhan University); Xiaochen Wang(Wuhan University); Yulin Wu(Jianghan University); Chenhao Hu(Xiaomi Corporation); Xueyang Lv(Xiaomi Corporation)
items.abstract: Speech super-resolution (SR) requires a delicate balance between preserving global harmonic coherence and sharp local transients. While diffusion-based models achieve impressive fidelity, their computational demands limit practical use; conversely, efficient time-domain architectures often struggle to capture the long-range spectral dependencies essential for precise harmonic alignment. We introduce STSR, an end-to-end MDCT-domain framework designed to bridge this gap. STSR leverages a Spectral-Contextual Attention mechanism with hierarchical windowing to aggregate non-local context, ensuring consistent harmonic restoration up to 48 kHz. To prevent the loss of transient clarity in compressed spectral representations, we incorporate a sparse-aware regularization strategy. Experimental results demonstrate that STSR surpasses state-of-the-art baselines in both perceptual quality and zero-shot generalization, establishing a robust, real-time paradigm for high-fidelity speech restoration. Samples can be found online.

items.title: A Novel Transfer Learning Approach for Room Impulse Response Estimation and Speech Dereverberation Across Geometrically Diverse and Data-Scarce Environments
items.authors: Shahab Pasha(Shahab Pasha, University of Western Australia); Jiahong Zhao(Jiahong Zhao, Institute of Sound and Vibration Research, University of Southampton); Hualin Ren(Hualin Ren, University of Wollongong); Christian Ritz(Christian Ritz, University of Wollongong)
items.abstract: Accurate Room Impulse Response estimation is critical for audio reproduction, echo cancellation, and speech dereverberation. Traditional methods are computationally expensive and generalize poorly across room shapes and materials. We propose a novel transfer learning framework that adapts models trained on data-rich rectangular rooms to L-shaped and irregular geometries with limited measurements. Our geometry-aware encoder extracts shape-invariant features, while a physics-informed decoder enforces echo sparsity and energy decay. Uniquely, we freeze the encoder during fine-tuning, updating only the decoder-achieving 56% lower MSE and 37% lower LSD on unseen target geometries with merely 10 training rooms. Downstream speech dereverberation validates practical utility with PESQ of 3.24 vs. 2.78 and STOI of 0.89 vs. 0.79 compared to Generative Adversarial Networks baselines.

items.title: HWB-plus: A Lightweight Speech Bandwidth Extension Method with Separate Modeling for Consonants and Vowels
items.authors: Xin Liu(Inner Mongolia University); Xueliang Zhang(Inner Mongolia University)
items.abstract: Speech Bandwidth Extension (BWE) aims to reconstruct the missing high-frequency components of narrowband signals for enhanced perceptual quality. However, existing methods often face a trade-off between performance and resource efficiency--a critical constraint for edge device deployment. This paper proposes an improved lightweight BWE approach based on HWB-Net, which achieves performance improvement with almost no change in model parameters and computational load. The key innovations are: (1) Dual-WGMM, grounded in STRAIGHT's periodic/aperiodic decomposition, including ConsWGMM (for high-frequency consonants) and VowelWGMM (for mid-to-low frequency vowels); (2) mel-scale initialization for VowelWGMM. Evaluated on the VCTK dataset, the proposed method outperforms SOTA lightweight models (HWB-Net, BAE-Lite) by significant margins across DNSMOS P.808, PESQ, and NISQA. This work provides a practical BWE solution for real-time communication on edge devices.

items.title: USDnet++: Distilling Signal Processing Based Dereverberation for Unsupervised Neural Speech Dereverberation
items.authors: Ruizhe Pang(Southern University of Science and Technology); Shulin He(Southern University of Science and Technology); Jingqi Sun(Southern University of Science and Technology); Zhong-Qiu Wang(Southern University of Science and Technology)
items.abstract: Given a set of unlabeled reverberant speech signals, the recent USDnet model can learn to effectively perform unsupervised single-speaker speech dereverberation. This paper proposes USDnet++, which extends USDnet by leveraging signal processing based dereverberation results to improve the training of USDnet. The rationale is that the dereverberation result produced by signal processing algorithms typically has a higher signal-to-noise (SNR) of the target speech and hence could be leveraged as a weak supervision to improve the training of USDnet. In this paper, we employ weighted prediction error (WPE) and convolutional beamforming (WPD) to derive the signal processing based dereverberation result for improving USDnet. Evaluation results on the WSJ0CAM-DEREVERB dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of USDnet++.

items.title: EffVOC: Low-Delay Efficient Speech Waveform Reconstruction from Spectral Representations Without Phase
items.authors: Renzheng Shi(TU Braunschweig); Simon Welker(Universität Hamburg); Timo Gerkmann(Universität Hamburg); Tim Fingscheidt(TU Braunschweig)
items.abstract: The Griffin-Lim algorithm has been a seminal contribution for phase reconstruction from amplitude spectrograms, however, requiring (infinitely) high algorithmic delay. Its low-delay variant suffers in speech quality. Recent (generative) neural network methods improve on speech quality still at medium to high algorithmic delay, but often they are complex and optimized only for one specific input representation. We build upon an efficient low-delay speech vocoder and propose EffVOC, which supports synthesis of wideband (WB) or fullband (FB) speech from either amplitude spectrum or Mel coefficient inputs. We evaluate both input representations across multiple model sizes in a unified framework and compare against state of the art. Results show that our proposed low-delay (20 ms vs. 32 ms or more) efficient approach marks a new SOTA by achieving top-ranked subjective MOS scores (WB: 4.17/4.15, FB: 4.14/4.11) for amplitude spectrum/Mel representations, very close to ground truth.

items.title: Your U-Net Dereverberation Model is Secretly an RIR Encoder
items.authors: Sina Khanagha(University of Hamburg); Timo Gerkmann(University of Hamburg)
items.abstract: In this work, we analyze the ability of NCSN++ U-Net based audio dereverberation models to capture global room characteristics in their intermediate representations. Through an empirical study of both a state-of-the-art diffusion-based model and a discriminative counterpart, we show that deeper layers encode structured room impulse response (RIR)-dependent embeddings. Moreover, the discriminative ability of this implicit room representation correlates with dereverberation performance across objective metrics. Motivated by this observation, we propose a training strategy that explicitly conditions the network on pre-trained RIR embeddings, obtained via self-supervised contrastive learning. Incorporating RIR conditioning improves representation quality, accelerates convergence, and enhances dereverberation performance, while significantly reducing the number of reverse diffusion steps required by the diffusion-based model during inference.

items.title: FastWave: Optimized Diffusion Model for Audio Super-Resolution
items.authors: Nikita Kuznetsov(HSE University; VK LLC); Maksim Kaledin(HSE University)
items.abstract: Audio Super-Resolution is a set of techniques aimed at high-quality estimation of the given signal as if it would be sampled with higher sample rate. Among suggested methods there are diffusion and flow models (which are considered slower), generative adversarial networks (which are considered faster), however both approaches are currently presented by high-parametric networks, requiring high computational costs both for training and inference. We propose a solution to both these problems by re-considering the recent advances in the training of diffusion models and applying them to super-resolution from any to 48 kHz sample rate. Our model called FastWave has around 50 GFLOPs of computational complexity and 1.3 M parameters and can be trained with less resources and significantly faster than the majority of recently proposed diffusion- and flow-based solutions. FastWave also has comparable performance to state-of-the-art models. We provide our implementation on GitHub.

items.title: LavaSR: Fast and Flexible Audio Bandwidth Extension via Vocos
items.authors: Yatharth Sharma(New York)
items.abstract: We propose a Vocos-based bandwidth extension model that enhances audio at 8–48 kHz by generating missing high-frequency content. Inputs are resampled to 48 kHz and processed by a neural vocoder backbone, enabling a single network to support arbitrary upsampling ratios. A lightweight Linkwitz-Riley-inspired refiner merges the original low band with the generated high frequencies via a smooth crossover. On validation, the model achieves competitive log-spectral distance while running at a real-time factor of 0.0001 on an NVIDIA A100 GPU and 0.0053 on an 8-core CPU, demonstrating practical, high-quality BWE at extreme throughput.

items.title: Adaptive Oscillatory Inductive Bias for Modeling Sharp Prosodic Dynamics in Diffusion-Based TTS
items.authors: Sandipan Dhar(Sony Research India); Nirmesh J. Shah(Sony Research India); Ashishkumar P. Gudmalwar(Sony Research India); Pankaj Wasnik(Sony Research India)
items.abstract: Diffusion-based text-to-speech (TTS) models have achieved significant improvements in speech quality. However, modeling sharp prosodic transitions and rapid pitch variations in expressive speech remains challenging. Existing diffusion-based TTS decoders commonly utilize periodic nonlinearities such as Snake activation function to capture harmonic structures, but this activation funcation provides limited adaptability when modeling abrupt amplitude and frequency variations. In this paper, we investigate the role of oscillatory inductive bias in diffusion-based TTS decoders and introduce an adaptive oscillatory nonlinearity that enables controllable periodic modulation while maintaining signal stability through a linear bypass component. We refer the resulting TTS system as OscillaTTS. Experiments on the LJSpeech and Emotional Speech Dataset show consistent improvements across objective and subjective evaluations, indicating improved modeling of expressive prosodic dynamics.

items.title: Word-level Emotional Intensity Control in TTS via Emotion Residual Vectors
items.authors: Ji-Hyun Park(Hanyang University); Nam-Seok Song(Hanyang University); Joon-Hyuk Chang(Hanyang University)
items.abstract: Modern emotional text-to-speech (TTS) models typically rely on utterance-level conditioning. However, natural emotional speech requires fine-grained variations across words to achieve nuanced, human-like expressiveness. To address this, we introduce emotion residual vectors (ERVs), which capture neutral-to-emotional deviations in word-aligned self-supervised speech embeddings as an annotation-free cue for local prosody. To stabilize intensity control, we compress ERVs into a low-dimensional bottleneck space and train a RoBERTa-based predictor to infer the projected vectors from text and emotion. During inference, the predicted vectors are converted into additive hidden-state offsets and injected into a neutral-conditioned TTS model, enabling continuous word-level intensity control. Experimental results show that our method improves local emotional controllability while preserving naturalness compared to controllable emotional TTS baselines.

items.title: Continuous Time-Varying Emotion Control Zero-Shot Text-To-Speech With Emotion Orthogonal LoRA
items.authors: Chenchen Wan(Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Minchuan Chen(Ping An Technology); Yan Shi(Ping An Technology); Peng Qi(Shanghai Jiao Tong University Chongqing Artificial Intelligence Research Institute); Shaojun Wang(Ping An Technology); Jing Xiao(Ping An Technology)
items.abstract: High-quality emotional text-to-speech (TTS) often depends on large scale corpora and coarse discrete emotion labels, which limits fine-grained and time-varying control in practice. We address this by integrating continuous Valence, Arousal, and Dominance (VAD) control into a pretrained model via low-rank updates inserted into the backbone transformations. Our Emotion Orthogonal LoRA (EO-LoRA) uses three separate low-rank branches aligned to valence, arousal, and dominance, and an orthogonality regularizer encourages the branches to capture distinct effects. We further introduce Flow-DGPO, a reinforcement learning alignment stage for flow matching TTS that improves emotion controllability while preserving intelligibility and speaker similarity. Experiments show that our method improves continuous and time-varying emotion control while maintaining synthesis quality with limited training data.

items.title: ETC-TTS: Emotion Trajectory Learning for Controllable Emotional Text-to-Speech
items.authors: Gaeun Kim(Hanyang University); Jaeuk Lee(Hanyang University); Joon-Hyuk Chang(Hanyang University)
items.abstract: Emotional text-to-speech (TTS) systems have achieved high speech quality, yet controllable emotion intensity modeling remains challenging. Existing approaches control emotion embeddings via scaling or interpolation at inference time, so intermediate emotional states are not explicitly learned. To address this limitation, we propose Emotion Trajectory learning for Controllable emotional TTS (ETC-TTS), a framework that models emotion intensity as continuous trajectories in latent style space. A residual vector quantization (RVQ)-based style extractor provides emotion-aware representations, and a flow-matching objective learns trajectories between neutral and target emotions. Unlike prior methods, ETC-TTS learns emotion transitions during training, enabling stable intensity control. Experiments on Korean and English datasets show improved controllability while preserving speech quality. Subjective and objective evaluations confirm more stable emotional expressions than baseline methods.

items.title: Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Personalized and Culturally Adaptive Emotional TTS via Interactive Optimization of Individual Emotion Perception Spaces
items.authors: Wangzixi Zhou(Nara Institute of Science and Technology); Bagus Tris Atmaja(Nara Institute of Science and Technology); Sakriani Sakti(Nara Institute of Science and Technology)
items.abstract: The rise of conversational AI has increased interest in emotional Text-to-Speech (TTS). Most systems rely on discrete emotion labels, which fail to capture the nuanced nature of human affect. Recent models employ dimensional representations such as Russell's arousal-valence (A-V) model, offering finer control. However, emotional perception varies across individuals and cultures, which may cause mismatches between modeled and perceived emotions. We propose a personalized and culturally adaptive emotional TTS framework that performs interactive optimization of individualized A-V perception spaces using an Interactive Genetic Algorithm. By adapting emotion representations to each listener, the system produces speech with more perceptually aligned emotional expression than models using averaged A-V values. Evaluations with Japanese, Chinese, and Indonesian participants highlight the importance of personalization and cultural adaptation for moving beyond one-size-fits-all emotional TTS.

items.title: Cross-modal Consistency Guidance for Robust Emotion Control in Auto-Regressive TTS Models
items.authors: Yizhou Peng(Nanyang Technological University); Yukun Ma(Alibaba); Chong Zhang(Alibaba); Yi-Wen Chao(Nanyang Technological University); Chongjia Ni(Alibaba); Bin Ma(Alibaba); Eng Siong Chng(Nanyang Technological University)
items.abstract: While Text-to-Speech (TTS) systems enable emotional control via natural-language instructions, expressiveness, naturalness, and speech quality degrade when the target emotion conflicts with the textual semantics. We propose a Cross-modal Consistency Guided Classifier-Free Guidance (CCG-CFG) method with dynamic scales based on the degree of inconsistency between the text emotion and the explicit speech emotion, replacing the dropout condition with the text emotion. We also distill the CCG-CFG guidance signal using a hard-sample mining strategy, improving the TTS model's emotional alignment capability. Evaluations on five emotional corpora and two TTS benchmarks show that our approaches applied to CosyVoice2 achieve up to a 12% absolute improvement in emotion-recognition accuracy and a 10% relative improvement in subjective scores, outperforming baselines including HierSpeech++, Qwen3-TTS, and the original CosyVoice2, while preserving intelligibility, naturalness, and high speech quality.

items.title: A Large-Scale Dataset of Listener Impressions of Emotional TTS
items.authors: Erica Cooper(National Institute of Information and Communications Technology); Xiaoxue Gao(A*STAR); Takuma Okamoto(National Institute of Information and Communications Technology); Tomoki Toda(Nagoya University; National Institute of Information and Communications Technology); Nancy Chen(A*STAR); Hisashi Kawai(National Institute of Information and Communications Technology)
items.abstract: We present the first large-scale dataset for speech quality assessment of emotional synthesized speech. The dataset consists of 18,208 speech samples in five emotional styles from 13 state-of-the-art synthesis systems and natural emotional speech, along with ratings from 262 listeners for quality and several aspects of emotional content, including perceived emotional categories, how well the speech matches the target emotion, valence, arousal, and dominance. Analyses of the ratings show the relationships between the different types of ratings, and experiments using pretrained emotion recognizers, speech quality predictors, and LLM-as-judge prediction approaches reveal reasonable correlations with human ratings in some cases, with room for improvement and varying results observed depending on the emotion category. This dataset will be made public to the research community as a resource for the developing automatic speech quality assessment models for emotional synthesized speech.

items.title: DECRA: Dynamic Emotion Control for Real-time Speech Anonymization
items.authors: Ghady Nasrallah(Texas A&M University); Waris Quamer(Texas A&M University); Mu-Ruei Tseng(Texas A&M University); Ricardo Gutierrez-Osuna(Texas A&M University)
items.abstract: Real-time speaker anonymization requires neutralizing or controlling emotional states with causal, low-latency synthesis to prevent leakage of sensitive paralinguistic information. However, most expressive VC systems operate offline and rely on global style conditioning, which limits real-time use and dynamic emotion control. In addition, speaker representations commonly used for VC entangle speaker identity with emotional attributes, making emotion control weaker and less reliable. We propose DECRA1, a real-time streaming VC system that performs closed-loop, time-varying prosody control. It conditions synthesis on continuous valence–arousal (VA) trajectories predicted online by a causal speech emotion recognition (SER) model, while disentangling speaker identity from emotion. The resulting system is streamable end-to-end, with <80 ms GPU latency. Experiments show improved VA-space emotion steering over SOTA baselines and demonstrate dynamic, time-varying emotion control.

items.title: Emo-BPO: Emotion Bidirectional Preference Optimization for Diffusion-based Emotional TTS
items.authors: Jiacheng Shi(William & Mary); Hongfei Du(William & Mary); Xinyuan Song(Emory University); Y. Alicia Hong(George Mason University); Yanfu Zhang(William & Mary); Ye Gao(William & Mary)
items.abstract: Diffusion-based TTS has demonstrated strong capability in emotional speech generation. However, existing emotion alignment methods primarily reinforce target emotional expressions while overlooking modeling of competing emotional modes, limiting fine-grained controllability. This issue becomes more pronounced under classifier-free guidance (CFG), which relies on contrasting conditional trajectories to shape generation. We propose Emotion Bidirectional Preference Optimization (Emo-BPO), a simple effective framework that jointly learns emotion-aligned and emotion-contrastive score functions from reordered same-text emotional pairs. Our method requires neither auxiliary reward models nor additional annotations, and can be seamlessly integrated into existing diffusion-based TTS systems to improve emotional controllability and expressiveness.

items.title: DeSRPA: Decoupled Speech Role-Playing Agent via Inference-Time Intervention
items.authors: Wenqiu Tang(Nagoya University); Zhen Wan(National Institute of Informatics); Takahiro Komamizu(Nagoya University); Ichiro Ide(Nagoya University)
items.abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized text-based role-playing, creating immersive Speech Role-Playing Agents (SRPAs) requires a seamless bridge between cognitive reasoning and paralinguistic nuances. Current SRPAs primarily rely on End-to-End (E2E) fine-tuning. However, this paradigm suffers from poor generalization to unseen characters due to its reliance on role-specific data, while imposing a “modality alignment tax” that degrades intrinsic LLM reasoning capabilities. We propose DeSRPA, an agentic framework for character role play via inference-time intervention on frozen backbones. It employs a dual-level Control Vector (CV) mechanism Internal Cognitive Steering and External Expressive Rendering to synchronize “mind” and “voice”. Experiments on SpeechRole and OmniCharacter benchmarks demonstrate that DeSRPA significantly outperforms E2E baselines in personality and emotional consistency. It achieves high speech naturalness, narrowing the gap with proprietary models like GPT-4o Audio, while remaining a scalable and training-free paradigm.

items.title: EmoInstruct-TTS: Dual-Path Instruction-Guided Emotional Speech Synthesis
items.authors: Minghui Wu(University of Science and Technology of China; iFLYTEK Research); Ganjun Liu(University of Science and Technology of China; iFLYTEK Research); Zikun Fang(University of Science and Technology of China); Ting Meng(iFLYTEK Research); Hongchuan Wu(iFLYTEK Research); Bingao Xu(iFLYTEK Research); Yonglong Cai(iFLYTEK Research); Jiasheng Chen(Huawei); Jun Du(University of Science and Technology of China)
items.abstract: Instruction-based controllable speech synthesis enables users to specify emotions through natural language. However, existing approaches often rely on coarse emotion labels and lack explicit modeling of fine-grained intensity. We propose EmoInstruct-TTS, a dual-path instruction-guided framework for emotional speech synthesis. We introduce Emotion2embed, a supervised semantic-acoustic emotion embedding covering 48 emotional states, including fine-grained categories and intensity levels. To infer embeddings from free-form instructions, we design an Instruction-Conditioned Emotion Flow Model (ICE-Flow) that generates acoustically grounded emotion representations. The inferred embeddings are integrated into an LLM-based synthesis pipeline to provide explicit emotional control while preserving semantic planning. Experiments show improved emotional controllability and speech naturalness over strong baselines.

items.title: ZeroSyl: Simple Zero-Resource Syllable Tokenization for Spoken Language Modeling
items.authors: Nicol Visser(Stellenbosch University); Simon Malan(Stellenbosch University); Danel Slabbert(Stellenbosch University); Herman Kamper(Stellenbosch University)
items.abstract: Pure speech language models aim to learn language directly from raw audio without textual resources. A key challenge is that discrete tokens from self-supervised speech encoders result in excessively long sequences, motivating recent work on syllable-like units. However, methods like Sylber and SyllableLM rely on intricate multi-stage training pipelines. We propose ZeroSyl, a simple training-free method to extract syllable boundaries and embeddings directly from a frozen WavLM model. Using L2 norms of features in WavLM's intermediate layers, ZeroSyl achieves competitive syllable segmentation performance. The resulting segments are mean-pooled, discretized using K-means, and used to train a language model. ZeroSyl outperforms prior syllabic tokenizers across lexical, syntactic, and narrative benchmarks. Scaling experiments show that while finer-grained units are beneficial for lexical tasks, our discovered syllabic units exhibit better scaling behavior for syntactic modeling.

items.title: Towards Data-free and Training-free Compression for Speech Foundation Models Using Parameter Clustering
items.authors: Haoning Xu(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Zhaoqing Li(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Huimeng Wang(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Youjun Chen(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Chengxi Deng(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Mengzhe Geng(National Research Council Canada); Xunying Liu(The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
items.abstract: This paper presents a novel data-free and training-free compression approach for speech foundation models using channel-wise clustering via k-means. More fine-grained, mixed sparsity pruning by layer-level varying number of parameter clusters is also explored. Experiments conducted on the LibriSpeech dataset suggest that when operating with pruning sparsity of 50% on HuBERT-large, consistent WER reductions of 27.73%/18.61% absolute (34.37%/21.91% relative) over the magnitude-based pruning were obtained on the test-clean and test-other subsets before fine-tuning and 0.19%/0.79% absolute (3.36%/4.62% relative) after fine-tuning with only 3 epochs. Similar WER reductions of 2.86%/5.02% absolute (59.21%/55.29% relative) were observed against magnitude-based pruning on Whisper-large-v3 at 10% sparsity, all with no significant WER increase relative to the uncompressed baseline.

items.title: OnDA: On-device Channel Pruning for Efficient Personalized Keyword Spotting
items.authors: Matteo Risso(Politecnico di Torino); Alessio Burello(Politecnico di Torino); Daniele Jahier Pagliari(Politecnico di Torino)
items.abstract: Always-on keyword spotting (KWS) demands on-device adaptation to cope with user- and environment-specific distribution shifts under tight latency and energy budgets. This paper proposes, for the first time, coupling weight adaptation (i.e., on-device training) with architectural adaptation, in the form of online structured channel pruning, for personalized on-device KWS. Starting from a state-of-the-art self-learning personalized KWS pipeline, we compare data-agnostic and data-aware pruning criteria applied on in-field pseudo-labelled user data. On the HeySnips and HeySnapdragon datasets, we achieve up to 9.63× model-size compression with respect to unpruned baselines at iso-task performance, measured as the accuracy at 0.5 false alarms per hour. When deploying our adaptation pipeline on a Jetson Orin Nano embedded GPU, we achieve up to 1.52×/1.57× and 1.64×/1.77× latency and energy-consumption improvements during online training/inference compared to weights-only adaptation.

items.title: Sub-Model Short-Term Memory Convolutions for Keyword Spotting Systems on Device
items.authors: Paweł Warlewski(Samsung R&D Institute Poland); Artur Czeczko(Samsung R&D Institute Poland); Artur Szumaczuk(Samsung R&D Institute Poland); Grzegorz Stefański(Samsung AI Center Warsaw); Szymon Klimaszewski(Samsung R&D Institute Poland)
items.abstract: Keyword Spotting (KWS) is becoming increasingly important as voice-controlled devices grow more widespread. While voice interaction with smartphones and smart TVs is already common, deploying KWS on heavily resource-constrained edge devices such as wearables remains challenging. These systems must meet high accuracy requirements while operating under strict constraints on computational power, memory footprint, and real-time latency. In this work, we present an application of the STMC (Short-Term Memory Convolutions) framework to adapt a modular CNN model for online, LSTM-like inference. Our approach reduces power consumption and redundant computations while maintaining the stability and simplicity of training CNNs. We achieve up to 82% and 46% MCPS reduction compared to equivalently frequent standard CNN execution and vanilla STMC, respectively. The best configuration achieves 93.8% accuracy on the 11-class Google Speech Commands task and 97.1% on the same task with zero-padded data.

items.title: An Efficient vLLM-Based Inference Pipeline for Unified Audio Understanding and Generation
items.authors: Haoran Wang(Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Carnegie Mellon University); Jinchuan Tian(Carnegie Mellon University); Siddhant Arora(Carnegie Mellon University); Shinji Watanabe(Carnegie Mellon University)
items.abstract: While Large Multimodal Models excel in comprehension, high-throughput inference engines lack native support for multimodal generation. This is severe in Speech Language Models, where generating multi-layered audio tokens via decoupled AR+NAR or synchronous Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) with delay-pattern interleaving conflicts with standard single-stream loops. We present a vLLM-based inference pipeline for unified speech understanding and generation. We extend autoregressive decoding to natively execute delay-pattern de-interleaving and coordinated multi-stream sampling, integrating an on-GPU acoustic decoder for end-to-end waveform synthesis. Crucially, we overcome the shared intuition that Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) halves throughput. By co-scheduling paired conditional and unconditional requests within a continuous batch, our CFG implementation sustains 80% of non-CFG throughput, absorbing dual-request and logit merging overheads. We open-source our framework1.

items.title: Audio-NSP: Data-Centric Semi-Autoregressive Generation for Large Audio-Language Models
items.authors: Liang Cao(Tsinghua University); Xize Cheng(Zhejiang University); Dongjie Fu(Zhejiang University); Weihao Wu(Tsinghua University); Fuming You(Tencent); Zhiyong Wu(Tsinghua University); Haifeng Hu(Tencent)
items.abstract: Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs) suffer from high latency due to the autoregressive decoding of long audio sequences. We propose Audio-NSP (Next Sequence Prediction), a framework that activates semi-autoregressive parallel generation in pre-trained LALMs solely through data-centric Supervised Fine-Tuning. By restructuring training sequences with blockwise attention, Audio-NSP enables simultaneous multi-token prediction without architectural modifications. Crucially, applying this to audio reveals a decoding dilemma caused by the entropy gap between deterministic text and highly variable audio tokens. To resolve this, we introduce a modality-aware dynamic truncation strategy. It applies strict thresholds for text and lenient thresholds for audio, preventing degeneration into single-step decoding while preserving fidelity. Experiments show Audio-NSP achieves speedups of up to 3.42x while significantly outperforming Multi-Token Prediction baselines in quality preservation.

items.title: Improving streaming ASR with foundation models using emission policies
items.authors: Gerard Mas Mollà(Universitat Politècnica de València); Albert Sanchis(Universitat Politècnica de València); Alfons Juan(Universitat Politècnica de València)
items.abstract: Speech Foundation Models (SFMs) have achieved state-of-the-art results in offline ASR, yet their application in streaming environments remains limited due to the performance degradation caused by restricted context. In this work, we propose a model-agnostic, training-free streaming pipeline designed to wrap around ASR models in a "black box" manner. Our approach integrates three key components: a sliding window audio buffer for incremental data ingestion, token-level timestamp management to eliminate redundant output, and text-only emission policies to govern output timing. We systematically evaluate several emission policies, assessing their impact on the latency-accuracy trade-off across three English datasets. Results show that our pipeline enables timestamp-producing SFMs like Parakeet and Canary to achieve near-offline transcription quality in real-time environments without requiring access to internal model tensors.

items.title: AdaTS: Adaptive Token Sampling for Efficient Speech Language Models
items.authors: Sonal Sannigrahi(Universidade de Lisboa; Instituto de Telecomunicações); Giuseppe Attanasio(Instituto de Telecomunicações); André F. T. Martins(Universidade de Lisboa; TransPerfect)
items.abstract: Speech Language Models (SLMs) have demonstrated strong speech understanding capabilities by incorporating speech tokens into large LMs (LLMs). However, most designs are i) token-intensive, as a large part of the LLM context is allotted to speech tokens, and ii) inefficient, as speech tokens are often temporally redundant, hindering SLMs’ capabilities to handle long-form tasks. To address both issues, we propose AdaTS, a dynamic sampling method that adaptively merges tokens where the speech signal is less informative. Our approach reduces the length of the speech signal seen by the LLM by 2× or more, with performance often better than standard downsampling across automatic speech recognition (ASR), speech question-answering (SQA), and speech translation (ST). Through an extensive empirical analysis, we show how SLMs using AdaTS retain strong speech understanding capabilities, while substantially reducing token redundancy and inference cost by 40%.

items.title: Merging the Knowledge of LLMs for Automatic Speech Recognition
items.authors: Hayato Futami(Kyoto University); Tatsuya Kawahara(Kyoto University)
items.abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems, trained on paired speech-text data, have been improved by leveraging language models (LMs) trained on text-only data. LM fusion methods such as shallow fusion and density ratio are well-established methods that incorporate external LMs during ASR decoding. However, they incur additional computational costs due to LM inference, which is particularly problematic for recent larger LMs. In this study, we propose incorporating external LMs via model merging. This method integrates the LMs directly into the parameters of an LLM-based ASR model, requiring no additional computational cost at inference. We formulate domain extension and transfer via arithmetic operations on LoRA parameters. Experimental evaluations were conducted for the domain adaptation of LLM-based ASR trained on CSJ and LibriSpeech. We show that our LM merging consistently improved the ASR performance in the target domains, without degrading inference speed or memory footprint.

items.title: Scaling few-shot spoken word classification with generative meta-continual learning
items.authors: Louise Beyers(Bytefuse); Batsirayi Mupamhi Ziki(Bytefuse); Ruan van der Merwe(Bytefuse)
items.abstract: Few-shot spoken word classification has largely been developed for applications where a small number of classes is considered, and so the potential of larger-scale few-shot spoken word classification remains untapped. This paper investigates the potential of a spoken word classifier to sequentially learn to distinguish between 1 000 classes when it is given only five shots per class. We demonstrate that this scaling capability exists by training a model using the Generative Meta-Continual Learning (GeMCL) algorithm and comparing it to repeatedly trained or finetuned baselines. We find that GeMCL produces exceptionally stable performance, and although it does not always outperform a repeatedly fully-finetuned HuBERT model nor a frozen HuBERT model with a repeatedly trained classifier head, it produces comparable performance to the latter while adapting 2 000 times faster, having been trained on less than half of the data for two orders of magnitude less time.

items.title: Hearing the Order: Investigating Position Bias in Large Audio-Language Models
items.authors: Yu-Xiang Lin(National Taiwan University); Chen-An Li(National Taiwan University); Sheng-Lun Wei(National Taiwan University); Po-Chun Chen(National Taiwan University); Hsin-Hsi Chen(National Taiwan University; NTU AI Research Center (AINTU)); Hung-yi Lee(National Taiwan University; NTU Artificial Intelligence Center of Research Excellence (NTU AI-CoRE))
items.abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) are often used in tasks that involve reasoning over ordered options. An open question is whether their predictions are influenced by the order of answer choices, which would indicate a form of position bias and undermine their reliability. In this paper, we identify and analyze this problem in LALMs. We demonstrate that no model is immune to this bias through extensive experiments on six LALMs across three widely used benchmarks and their spoken counterparts. Shuffling the order of answer options can cause performance fluctuations of up to 24% and even change model rankings, raising concerns about the reliability of current evaluation practices. We also study permutation-based strategies and show that they can mitigate bias in most cases. Our work represents the first systematic investigation of this issue in LALMs, and we hope it raises awareness and motivates further research in this direction.

items.title: Nudging Hidden States: Training-Free Model Steering for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Large Audio-Language Models
items.authors: Lok-Lam Ieong(National Taiwan University); Chia-Chien Chen(National Taiwan University); Chih-Kai Yang(National Taiwan University); Yu-Han Huang(National Taiwan University); An-Yu Cheng(National Taiwan University); Hung-yi Lee(National Taiwan University)
items.abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting has been extended to large audio-language models (LALMs) to elicit reasoning, yet enhancing its effectiveness without training remains challenging. We study inference-time model steering as a training-free approach to improve LALM reasoning. We introduce three strategies using diverse information sources and evaluate them across four LALMs and four benchmarks. Results show general accuracy gains up to 4.4% over CoT prompting. Notably, we identify a cross-modal transfer where steering vectors derived from few text samples effectively guide speech-based reasoning, demonstrating high data efficiency. We also examine hyperparameter sensitivity to understand the robustness of these approaches. Our findings position model steering as a practical direction for strengthening LALM reasoning.

items.title: MUGEN: Evaluating and Improving Multi-audio Understanding of Large Audio-Language Models
items.authors: Chih-Kai Yang(National Taiwan University); Yun-Shao Tsai(National Taiwan University); Yu-Kai Guo(National Taiwan University); Ping-Le Tsai(National Taiwan University); Yen-Ting Piao(National Taiwan University); Hung-Wei Chen(National Taiwan University); Ting-Lin Hsiao(National Taiwan University); Yun-Man Hsu(National Taiwan University); Ke-Han Lu(National Taiwan University); Hung-yi Lee(NTU AI-CoRE)
items.abstract: While multi-audio understanding is critical for large audio-language models (LALMs), it remains underexplored. We introduce MUGEN, a comprehensive benchmark evaluating this capability across speech, general audio, and music. Our experiments reveal consistent weaknesses in multi-audio settings, and performance degrades sharply as the number of concurrent audio inputs increases, identifying input scaling as a fundamental bottleneck. We further investigate training-free strategies and observe that Audio-Permutational Self-Consistency, which diversifies the order of audio candidates, helps models form more robust aggregated predictions, yielding up to 6.28% accuracy gains. Combining this permutation strategy with Chain-of-Thought further improves performance to 6.74%. These results expose blind spots in current LALMs and provide a foundation for evaluating complex auditory comprehension.

items.title: From Noisy Speech to Accurate APIs: LLM-driven Embedding Steering for Resilient Tool Retrieval
items.authors: Catalin Zorilă(Toshiba Europe Ltd); Qingxiuxiong Dong(Toshiba Corporation); Rama Doddipatla(Toshiba Europe Ltd)
items.abstract: Embedding-based tool retrieval is challenging and often fails in real deployments because API descriptors are inconsistent to what the embedding models are originally trained with and often require fine-tuning or retraining from scratch. The challenge is further amplified in speech driven queries, where background noise can degrade automatic speech recognition (ASR) outputs. We present a training free offline method that leverages an LLM to generate diverse, user-style synthetic queries, tasks, and scenarios for each tool, and then average (or steer) the embeddings to form a semantically enriched tool representation. To evaluate the robustness, we simulate realistic speech conditions-including reverberation and additive noise prior to ASR- and present experiments using multiple embedding models and tool datasets. Our results show that the proposed method provides a simple yet effective way to enhance tool retrieval reliability without requiring any model retraining.

items.title: A Reranker for Orchestrating Heterogeneous Speech and Text Retrievers
items.authors: Inho Kim(Korea Institute of Energy Technology); Sumyeong Ahn(Korea Institute of Energy Technology)
items.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems have attracted significant interest for their ability to mitigate hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs). Although knowledge databases for RAG are increasingly diversifying to include various modalities such as speech and text, research on handling such multi-modal database scenarios remains limited. In this paper, we propose STEREO (Speech and Text Reranking Orchestrator), a reranker based on speech and text retrievers that aggregates disparate modality databases. To address the lack of specialized training data, we first curate a dataset comprising queries, mixed-modality evidence, and their corresponding relevance ranks. We then train the reranker and evaluate its effectiveness in both single-modality and mixed-modality scenarios. Our results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm excels at selecting the most relevant evidence, thereby significantly improving downstream question-answering performance.

items.title: Do What I Say: A Spoken Prompt Dataset for Instruction-Following
items.authors: Maike Züfle(Karlsruhe Institute of Technology); Sara Papi(Fondazione Bruno Kessler); Fabian Retkowski(Karlsruhe Institute of Technology); Szymon Mazurek(ACC Cyfronet AGH, AGH University of Krakow); Marek Kasztelnik(ACC Cyfronet AGH); Alexander Waibel(Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Carnegie Mellon University); Luisa Bentivogli(Fondazione Bruno Kessler); Jan Niehues(Karlsruhe Institute of Technology)
items.abstract: Speech Large Language Models (SLLMs) have rapidly expanded, supporting a wide range of tasks. These models are typically evaluated using text prompts, which may not reflect real-world scenarios where users interact with speech. To address this gap, we introduce DoWhatISay (DOWIS), a multilingual dataset of human-recorded spoken and written prompts designed to pair with any existing benchmark for realistic evaluation of SLLMs under spoken instruction conditions. Spanning 9 tasks and 11 languages, it provides 10 prompt variants per task-language pair, across five styles. Using DOWIS, we benchmark state-of-the-art SLLMs, analyzing the interplay between prompt modality, style, language, and task type. Results show that text prompts consistently outperform spoken prompts, particularly for low-resource and cross-lingual settings. Only for tasks with speech output, spoken prompts do close the gap, highlighting the need for speech-based prompting in SLLM evaluation.

items.title: All That Glitters Is Not Audio: Rethinking Text Priors and Audio Reliance in Audio-Language Evaluation
items.authors: Leonardo Haw-Yang Foo(National Taiwan University); Chih-Kai Yang(National Taiwan University); Chen-An Li(National Taiwan University); Ke-Han Lu(National Taiwan University); Hung-yi Lee(National Taiwan University)
items.abstract: Large Audio-Language Models show consistent performance gains across speech and audio benchmarks, yet high scores may not reflect true auditory perception. If a model can answer questions without processing the acoustic signal, the benchmark fails as a measure of auditory understanding. We present a diagnostic framework using two axes: text prior, which measures answerability from text and general knowledge alone, and audio reliance, which assesses actual dependency on the acoustic signal. Evaluating eight LALMs across three benchmarks, we find that models retain 60-72% of their full-audio scores even without any audio input. Moreover, among items that require audio, only 3.0-4.2% need the complete audio clip; the majority can be resolved using localized fragments. These findings challenge the assumption that benchmark performance equals robust audio understanding, and we conclude with practical guidelines for improving evaluation reliability and benchmark design.

items.title: ADALA: A Wake-up Word Detection Framework Based on Adaptive Semi-supervised learning and Large Language Model
items.authors: Nianhang Tang(HUST; National Engineering Research Center of Digital Home Networking); Chaoyi Sun(HUST); Chao Cai(HUST)
items.abstract: The efficacy of Wake-up Word (WUW) detection is often constrained by poor generalization to unseen negative samples, exacerbating the trade-off between wake-up rate and false activation rate. To address this limitation, we introduce ADALA, a novel WUW detection framework that integrates ADAptive semi-supervised learning with a LArge language model. Specifically, a Large Language Model (LLM) is fine-tuned via Reinforcement Learning (RL) to dynamically generate new and effective hard-negative samples. These synthetically generated negatives are subsequently combined with real-world data within a semi-supervised learning scheme to continuously enhance the WUW model. Experimental results validate our approach, demonstrating that ADALA achieves a superior performance equilibrium, significantly reducing the false activation rate (3.19%) on datasets of phonetically similar words while preserving a high wake-up rate (90.43%).

items.title: Said Aloud, Read Different: Cross-Modal Instability in Multimodal Models
items.authors: Basel Mousi(HBKU); Fahim Dalvi(HBKU); Shammur Absar Chowdhury(HBKU); Firoj Alam(HBKU); Nadir Durrani(HBKU)
items.abstract: Multimodal foundation models are increasingly used in speech-first assistants that must interpret spoken queries and produce visually grounded decisions. Yet it remains unclear whether semantically equivalent queries yield consistent judgments across modality (text vs. speech) and language (English vs. Arabic). We introduce a speech-augmented visually grounded contrastive triplet benchmark spanning 10,150 culturally grounded images from 18 MENA countries, where each image is paired with one supported statement and two plausible but unsupported alternatives. We define contrastive instability as the conditional rate at which a model fails to resolve all statements within a triplet, isolating fragmented reasoning from complete failure. Evaluating recent multimodal models under text and speech in English and Arabic, we find that modality and language shifts introduce substantial triplet-level inconsistencies that are not fully captured by aggregate accuracy, with speech amplifying partial failures. We make the benchmark publicly available to the community.

items.title: When Does Quality-Aware Multimodal Fusion Matter? A Leakage-Safe Diagnostic for Decision-Level Dependence
items.authors: Jaden Moon(Dartmouth College); Arvind Pillai(Dartmouth College); Andrew Campbell(Dartmouth College)
items.abstract: Many multimodal systems estimate the reliability of each modality and weight their contributions to the final prediction. However, it remains unclear whether these scores influence model decisions or merely correlate with performance. We propose a simple diagnostic to test whether reliability information is used during inference. After training, the model and inputs are fixed while reliability scores are permuted across test examples. If predictions depend on these scores, performance should degrade. Experiments on StressID for stress recognition and CMU-MOSEI for sentiment analysis show that permuting reliability scores leaves performance unchanged despite substantial potential gains from selecting the best modality per example. In positive controls where reliability signals identify the correct modality, the same frozen fusion rules yield significant improvements, indicating that reliability signals influence fused decisions only when they reliably predict unimodal correctness.
